repository.name: thermoweave-battery-digital-twin
repository.title: ThermoWeave Spatial Battery Lab
repository.description: Review graph-based battery electrothermal dynamics, cooling assumptions and reproducible evidence in MATLAB experiments.
repository.summary: ThermoWeave models a synthetic battery assembly with thermal graphs, spatial boundaries, control, and deterministic fault studies. This companion introduces a one-node balance before the native multi-node experiments.
repository.audience: Battery thermal researchers and MATLAB learners studying topology, cooling boundaries, and numerical verification.

model.equation: ΔT = (Q/h) · (1 − exp(−h · 60t/C)); T = Tₐ + ΔT; heat removed = hΔT; stored heat = CΔT/1000.
assumptions: One uniform thermal mass starts at ambient temperature.
Constant heat input and linear heat transfer; no phase change or spatial gradients.
Elapsed time is shown in minutes; the energy-balance calculation uses seconds.
ThermoWeave is an independent synthetic MATLAB implementation with source-controlled provenance; third-party product rights remain separate.
The browser’s illustrative node is not a fitted cell and its visual assembly is not a calculated spatial temperature field.
Native kelvin-based graph experiments and optional Simscape gates remain separate from this Celsius-based one-node lesson.
model.introduction: The browser shows one scalar thermal balance with invented parameters. It cannot reproduce ThermoWeave’s temperature field, graph topology, coolant propagation, faults, controllers, or scenario-hashed native artifacts.

modules.title: Identify one node’s energy balance
modules.objective: Read a local thermal balance before adding graph interfaces.
steps: Read the signs, units, and node-state orientation in docs/model.md.
Apply 600 W heat, 30 W/K cooling, 12,000 J/K capacity, and 20°C ambient.
Predict a 20 K steady rise and inspect the ten-minute temperature and stored heat.

checkpoints.label: One-node stored heat after ten minutes

modules.reflection: Which inter-node heat-flow terms disappear when a graph is reduced to one uniform thermal mass?

modules.title: Change the boundary conductance
modules.objective: Explain how a boundary parameter affects both steady rise and transient response.
steps: Hold heat, capacity, and ambient fixed.
Double the cooling conductance from 30 to 60 W/K and predict the ten-minute response.
Read the scalar, vector, zonal, and coolant boundary distinctions in the native model documentation.
modules.reflection: Why is replacing a scalar boundary with per-cell values a model-structure change rather than simply another value on this slider?

modules.title: Locate the limit of a pack average
modules.objective: Identify why a single temperature cannot reveal spatial hot spots.
steps: Return conductance to 30 W/K and raise ambient to 35°C.
Run and compare the absolute temperature with the unchanged rise above ambient.
Open the native 3D study source and identify the topology and conductance information the browser does not contain.

checkpoints.label: Hot-boundary scalar temperature after ten minutes
Stored heat above ambient remains the baseline value

modules.reflection: What measurements or spatially resolved states would be required to make a claim about cell-to-cell temperature spread?

modules.title: Design a reproducible graph experiment
modules.objective: Carry a scalar intuition into a native study with explicit topology and evidence checks.
steps: Use the hot-boundary case and double thermal capacity to 24,000 J/K.
Predict the slower ten-minute response and export its assumptions.
Write a native study plan specifying graph dimensions, conductances, boundary mode, solver settings, seed, source revision, and energy-accounting checks.

checkpoints.label: Higher-inertia scalar temperature after ten minutes
Residual net heating after ten minutes

modules.reflection: Why would reproducible scenario hashes and small energy residuals still not establish predictive accuracy for a physical battery?
